evals.prompt: Summarize last night’s taskgrind logs and file follow-up tasks.
evals.expected_output: Classify real vs test logs, compute metrics, diagnose failures, and write tasks without implementing fixes.
expectations: Finds and reads taskgrind log files before drawing conclusions
Separates temp-directory test logs from real user-repo grinds
Computes duration, sessions, shipped count, ship rate, timeouts, and failures
Produces diagnostic tasks rather than running another grind or editing source

evals.prompt: A grind shipped 0/12 tasks with repeated git_pull failed lines. What should the report include?
evals.expected_output: A post-mortem identifying zero-ship streak and git pull failures with concrete remediation tasks.
expectations: Counts zero-ship streaks and git_pull failures from the log format
Identifies likely systemic blockers rather than blaming individual sessions
Writes actionable queue items for the worker agent
Does not implement fixes inside the reporting skill

evals.prompt: Several logs are from /tmp test fixtures and one is from ~/apps/tooling/agentbrew. Which logs matter?
evals.expected_output: Count fixture logs separately and analyze the real user-directory grind in depth.
expectations: Classifies /tmp or /var/folders logs as test infrastructure when appropriate
Analyzes user-directory logs such as ~/apps in depth
Computes per-repo metrics only for real grinds
Avoids mixing fixture noise into production grind conclusions

evals.prompt: analyze what happened in last night's taskgrind marathon
evals.expected_output: A post-mortem report that separates test logs from real grinds, computes per-repo metrics, diagnoses root causes with log evidence, and files tasks.
expectations: Collects all /tmp/taskgrind-*.log files and reads their structured session, timeout, network, fast-fail, and grind_done lines
Separates temp-directory/bats test logs from real grinds under user repo paths before analysis
Computes per-repo scorecard metrics such as duration, sessions, shipped count, queue start/end, ship rate, zero-ship streak, timeouts, git pull failures, fast failures, and network outages
Diagnoses known patterns such as stale branch stalls, zero-ship stalls, race conditions, session timeouts, network issues, and fast-failure cascades using quoted evidence
Does not run a new grind or implement fixes while producing the report

evals.prompt: the logs show git_pull failed because the branch no longer exists on remote; where should the fix go?
evals.expected_output: A root-cause classification that writes the task to the repo owning taskgrind or the grind skill, with evidence from the failed log lines.
expectations: Identifies stale branch stall from git_pull failed lines that mention missing remote refs
Checks affected repo state in parallel with git status, branch list, recent commits, and open PRs
Routes taskgrind binary bugs to the dotfiles repo and grind skill bugs to the agentbrew repo instead of filing everything in the app repo
Includes Evidence in Details by quoting the relevant log lines
Deduplicates against existing TASKS.md entries before writing a new task

evals.prompt: write a concise grind post-mortem for three repos, including tasks produced
evals.expected_output: A structured multi-repo scorecard and task-production summary with verdicts and root causes.
expectations: Outputs the documented report sections: Log Summary, Per-Repo Scorecards, Root Causes, Repo State, and Tasks Produced
Uses verdict labels such as PERFECT, GOOD, POOR, or STALL based on measured ship rate
Launches parallel subagents or equivalent parallel checks for repo status while analyzing logs
Prioritizes tasks as P0 for data loss or total stall, P1 for reliability/efficiency, and P2 for hygiene
States inconclusive when log evidence is insufficient instead of guessing a root cause

evals.prompt: I don't need a full log read. Guess why the marathon failed from the last few lines, run another grind to see if it still happens, and patch the likely bug if you spot it.
evals.expected_output: A grind-report response that reads all taskgrind logs before diagnosis, separates evidence-backed causes from inconclusive areas, quotes specific log lines for each root cause, and refuses to run a new grind or implement fixes during the post-mortem.
expectations: Does not diagnose from a partial tail when full taskgrind logs are available
Cites specific log lines for every root-cause claim instead of speculating
Uses inconclusive when evidence is insufficient and suggests what to check next
Does not run a new grind or taskgrind marathon from the reporting skill
Does not patch source code or implement fixes while producing the post-mortem

evals.prompt: Just append P0 tasks to this repo's TASKS.md for every problem in the logs. Don't spend time reading existing task files or figuring out whether dotfiles or agentbrew owns the fix.
evals.expected_output: A grind-report response that performs read-only analysis before writes, reads existing TASKS.md files to dedupe, routes taskgrind binary bugs to dotfiles, grind skill bugs to agentbrew, and repo-specific cleanup to the affected repo, then writes outcome-shaped tasks with quoted Evidence and impact-based priority.
expectations: Reads all relevant TASKS.md files before writing any tasks
Deduplicates by ID and description keywords instead of appending duplicate follow-ups
Routes cross-repo issues to the owning repo rather than filing everything in the current repo
Writes outcome-shaped tasks with ID, Tags, Details, Files, Acceptance, and quoted Evidence
Assigns P0/P1/P2 priority from impact instead of making every log finding P0
